title: The first verified patch and integrated startup

steps.title: Run and preserve baseline verification checks
deliverables: A verification-command profile with provenance and adapters for the fixture's real parser/compiler and behavioral test commands.
Baseline execution records containing test identities, definition digests, environment, statuses, and already present failures.
acceptance: The faulty fixture baseline records its known failing behavior and an unrelated pre-existing failure as separate observations.
An unavailable test dependency becomes blocked or infrastructure_error, while an unexecuted configured check remains not_run instead of passing by default.
steps.notes: Validate discovered commands through the existing tool gateway. Use stable behavior/test identities plus definition digests so a later edited test is not automatically treated as comparable baseline evidence.

steps.title: Define bounded coding handoffs and a scripted producer
deliverables: An immutable implementation-contract record binding the task contract, base state, change scope, expected behavior, and required checks.
A scripted model-adapter fixture returning either a patch artifact or a classified inability, with invocation identity and assumptions.
acceptance: The scripted fixture produces a patch without a real model and persists the exact manually assembled input packet, deployment identity, and invocation links through the common contracts.
A response containing both patch and inability, an unknown contract, or a mismatched base is rejected before candidate creation.
steps.notes: Use explicit scripted deployment metadata and report it honestly. The real model gateway can implement the same contract later; this fixture establishes handoff semantics rather than model capability. Include the scoped reuse/adapt/build assessment and available library/tool/workflow search receipts. In the scripted milestone these are supplied fixtures; P176 later executes production discovery.

steps.title: Apply candidate patches against their declared base
deliverables: A candidate-application operation checking the recorded base, mutation lease, permitted paths, and patch artifact before applying it in an isolated workspace.
Candidate records linking the coding result, exact base, resulting state, and patch artifact, including explicit import provenance.
acceptance: The fixture repair applies to its expected state and produces a new recorded state while leaving the source workspace unchanged.
The same patch against a changed base or outside permitted paths produces state_mismatch or scope denial and cannot create an apparently successful candidate.
steps.notes: Imported branch changes remain explicit application actions. Application success only establishes patch applicability; every resulting candidate still requires verification on its own state.

steps.title: Assess candidate criteria using exact-state verification
deliverables: A criterion-assessment service consuming current-contract checks and candidate executions with passed, failed, blocked, not_run, inconclusive, or infrastructure statuses.
Baseline-versus-candidate comparison that exposes changed test definitions and limits each observation to the behavior it covers.
acceptance: A passing result from one fixture branch or environment cannot satisfy a criterion on another; the candidate's own checks are required.
The known baseline failure is distinguished from a newly introduced regression, and an agent-authored passing test does not mark unrelated requirements verified.
Removing or weakening a configured check is visible and cannot silently produce a passing acceptance gate.

steps.title: Export the selected patch with an immutable verification manifest
deliverables: Manifest assembly recording candidate, patch, base/result states, environment, current contract, check definitions, executions, criterion statuses, and limitations.
Candidate inspection and result-export operations returning the selected artifacts, actual participating deployments, and explicit final outcome.
acceptance: An exported manifest resolves to the exact patch and execution artifacts used for the selected candidate; altered artifact bytes fail integrity validation.
A candidate with an unresolved mandatory criterion exports as partial or blocked under policy, with unexecuted checks visible rather than a verified success.
steps.notes: Returning a patch does not apply it to the user's workspace or invoke an external publication capability. Preserve the selected result even when disposable candidate workspaces are later removed.

steps.title: Complete a scripted task-to-patch vertical slice
deliverables: A deterministic controller path connecting submission, initialization, baseline checks, scripted coding handoff, patch application, verification, and final export.
An end-to-end fixture exercising restart boundaries and recording all work through the existing event and budget paths.
acceptance: A clean run returns a patch that applies to a fresh fixture checkout and passes the documented checks without changing the original repository.
Importing a fixture patch into another candidate requires fresh verification; the source branch's passing record cannot complete the import.
Changing a requirement before finalization creates reassessment work and prevents success under the obsolete contract.
steps.notes: The scripted producer is the only model participant; report no real-model capability claim.
